# facebookresearch/esmsparkPowered by Gemini

# facebookresearch/esmsparkPowered by Gemini

Updated onAug 9, 2026Commit[`2b36991`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/tree/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac)Gemini can make mistakes, so double\-check it\.![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This repository provides models and tools for protein sequence and structure analysis, prediction, and design\. It leverages Transformer\-based language models to generate protein representations, predict 3D structures, and engineer novel protein sequences\. The software enables a range of computational biology tasks, from understanding protein function to developing new protein\-based therapeutics\.

 The repository offers distinct capabilities addressing key areas of protein science:

 - **Protein Language Models** apply Transformer architectures to analyze protein sequences, generating rich representations for various downstream tasks\. These models include ESM\-2 for general sequence analysis, MSA Transformer for multiple sequence alignments, and ESM\-1v for zero\-shot variant prediction\. [Protein Language Models](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#protein-language-models) describes these models\.
- **Protein 3D Structure Prediction** utilizes ESMFold to predict a protein's three\-dimensional shape directly from its amino acid sequence\. ESMFold integrates language model embeddings with folding mechanisms, also providing quality metrics for predicted structures\. More details are available in [Protein 3D Structure Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#protein-3d-structure-prediction)\.
- **Inverse Folding for Protein Design** employs models like ESM\-IF1 to generate protein sequences that can adopt a specified 3D structure\. This capability supports both sampling novel sequences and scoring existing ones based on their structural compatibility\. [Inverse Folding for Protein Design](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#inverse-folding-for-protein-design) explains this process\.
- **Example Applications and Tutorials** demonstrate practical uses of these models, including generative protein design frameworks and techniques for large model inference\. These resources guide researchers in applying the models to their own work\. See [Example Applications and Tutorials](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#example-applications-and-tutorials) for details\.
- **ESM Metagenomic Atlas** provides a large database of pre\-computed protein structures and embeddings derived from metagenomic data\. This resource enables broad structural and functional analysis across millions of proteins\. [ESM Metagenomic Atlas](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#esm-metagenomic-atlas) describes how to access and use this data\.## Protein Language Models

| Model Name | File Path | Primary Purpose | Key Predictions/Functionality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ProteinBertModel \(ESM\-1, ESM\-1b\) | esm/model/esm1\.py | Protein sequence representation learning | Sequence embeddings, Contact prediction, Masked language modeling |
| ESM2 | esm/model/esm2\.py | Protein sequence representation learning with improved architecture | Sequence embeddings, Contact prediction, Masked language modeling |
| MSATransformer | esm/model/msa\_transformer\.py | Protein MSA representation learning | MSA embeddings, Contact prediction, Masked language modeling |
| GVPTransformerModel | esm/inverse\_folding/gvp\_transformer\.py | Inverse protein folding | Generates protein sequences given a 3D backbone structure |
| ESMFold | esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold\.py | End\-to\-end protein structure prediction | 3D protein structure prediction, Predicted lDDT \(pLDDT\), Predicted TM\-score \(pTM\), Predicted aligned error \(PAE\) |

The repository provides a collection of Transformer\-based protein language models designed for various protein sequence and structure prediction tasks\. These models learn patterns and relationships from vast datasets of protein sequences, enabling them to generate representations useful for understanding protein function, predicting structure, and designing novel proteins\.

 The core models include:

 - **ESM\-2** \([`esm/model/esm2.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm2.py)\): An advanced Transformer model that generates sequence embeddings, masked language modeling \(MLM\) predictions, and contact predictions\.
- **ESMFold** \([`esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py)\): An end\-to\-end model that integrates ESM language model embeddings with a folding mechanism to predict 3D protein structures directly from amino acid sequences\. This model predicts not only the structure but also quality metrics like pLDDT and pTM scores\.
- **MSA Transformer** \([`esm/model/msa_transformer.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/msa_transformer.py)\): A specialized model designed to process Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\)\. It utilizes axial self\-attention to capture evolutionary information across aligned sequences, performing masked language modeling and contact prediction tailored for MSA contexts\.
- **ESM\-1v** \([`esm/model/esm1.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm1.py)\): A variant of the ESM\-1b model optimized for zero\-shot prediction of variant effects, enabling the assessment of how mutations might impact protein function\.
- **ESM\-IF1** \([`esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer.py)\): An inverse folding model that predicts protein sequences given a 3D protein structure\. This is particularly useful for generative protein design and for scoring the likelihood of sequences against a known structure\.

 These models are accessible through various loading mechanisms, including the [README\.md?plain=1 L159](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L159) entry point defined in [`hubconf.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/hubconf.py), which offers convenience functions for direct loading of specific pre\-trained model variants like [pretrained\.py L374](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L374), [pretrained\.py L411](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L411), [pretrained\.py L281](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L281), and [pretrained\.py L339](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L339)\. The [pretrained\.py L24](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L24) function in [`esm/pretrained.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py) handles the underlying logic for downloading and loading these models and their associated [data\.py L91](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L91) for tokenization\.

 For practical use, utility scripts like [`scripts/extract.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/extract.py) facilitate the extraction of sequence representations, while [`scripts/fold.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py) handles 3D protein structure prediction using ESMFold\. [Data Handling and Pre\-trained Model Loading](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#protein-language-models-data-handling-and-pre-trained-model-loading) provides further details on how data is prepared for these models\. The repository also includes example applications demonstrating how to use these models for tasks such as generative design and variant prediction [Example Applications and Tutorials](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#example-applications-and-tutorials)\.### ESM\-1b and ESM\-2 Architectures and Core Functionality

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ESM\-1b and ESM\-2 models are Transformer\-based protein language models designed for tasks such as generating sequence embeddings, masked language modeling \(MLM\), and predicting inter\-residue contacts\. These models process protein sequences to create representations that are useful for diverse downstream applications\.

 The core of both models is the Transformer architecture, which consists of multiple [modules\.py L84](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L84) blocks\. These blocks incorporate multi\-head self\-attention mechanisms and feed\-forward networks to capture complex dependencies within protein sequences\. Positional information is injected into the token embeddings using either [modules\.py L224](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L224) \(for ESM\-1b\) or [modules\.py L260](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L260) \(for ESM\-1\) to account for the order of amino acids in a sequence\. ESM\-2 further enhances this with [modules\.py L94](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L94) for improved positional encoding\.

 For masked language modeling, both models employ a [modules\.py L298](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L298) \(in [`esm/model/esm1.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm1.py) and [`esm/model/esm2.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm2.py)\) to predict masked amino acids based on their context\. This pre\-training objective enables the models to learn generalizable protein sequence semantics\. ESM\-1b's [modules\.py L298](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L298) can share weights with the initial token embedding layer for parameter efficiency\.

 Contact prediction, which infers physical contacts between residues, is integrated into both ESM\-1b and ESM\-2 through a [modules\.py L317](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L317) \(in [`esm/model/esm1.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm1.py) and [`esm/model/esm2.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm2.py)\)\. This component typically utilizes attention weights from the Transformer layers to derive contact probabilities, providing insights into protein structure\.

 The models are initialized with an [data\.py L91](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L91) object \(in [`esm/model/esm1.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm1.py) and [`esm/model/esm2.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm2.py)\) that defines the vocabulary of amino acids and special tokens\. Their [modules\.py L57](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L57) methods are designed to be flexible, allowing users to retrieve not only the masked language model predictions \([esm1\.py L32](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm1.py#L32)\) but also intermediate hidden representations \([README\.md?plain=1 L183](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L183)\) from specified layers and attention weights \([modules\.py L338](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L338)\)\. This configurability makes the models versatile for various research tasks requiring detailed insights into sequence features or protein dynamics\.

 ESM\-2, implemented in [`esm/model/esm2.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm2.py), builds upon the Transformer design with specific enhancements like [modules\.py L94](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L94) and [modules\.py L71](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L71) for layer normalization, which contribute to its performance in generating contextualized embeddings\. For example, the [modules\.py L57](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L57) method in [`esm/model/esm2.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm2.py) collects hidden representations and attention weights, enabling comprehensive analysis of the protein sequence\.### MSA Transformer for Multiple Sequence Alignments

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The MSA Transformer is a specialized model designed to process Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), which are crucial for understanding protein evolution and function\. Its architecture is built upon the Transformer design, adapted to leverage the two\-dimensional nature of MSAs, where rows represent different sequences and columns represent aligned positions\. This enables the model to capture evolutionary information from a collection of related protein sequences\.

 Central to the MSA Transformer's design is the concept of axial self\-attention, which allows the model to efficiently process the complex relationships within an MSA\. Instead of performing attention over the entire MSA simultaneously, which can be computationally intensive, axial self\-attention decomposes this into two independent operations: row\-wise attention and column\-wise attention\. This is implemented through the [modules\.py L145](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L145) \(defined in [`esm/model/msa_transformer.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/msa_transformer.py)\), which orchestrates the application of both [axial\_attention\.py L11](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/axial_attention.py#L11) and [axial\_attention\.py L133](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/axial_attention.py#L133) modules\.

 The [axial\_attention\.py L11](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/axial_attention.py#L11) module \(found in [`esm/axial_attention.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/axial_attention.py)\) computes self\-attention along each sequence independently, capturing dependencies between amino acid residues within a single protein sequence\. Conversely, the [axial\_attention\.py L133](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/axial_attention.py#L133) module \(also in [`esm/axial_attention.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/axial_attention.py)\) performs self\-attention across the aligned positions, integrating information across different sequences for a given amino acid position\. This dual attention mechanism allows the MSA Transformer to build rich representations that encompass both individual sequence characteristics and evolutionary conservation patterns\.

 The model is configured to handle various protein language modeling tasks\. For instance, it performs masked language modeling \(MLM\) by predicting masked amino acids within the MSA, akin to how general language models predict missing words in text\. This process helps the model learn contextual representations of amino acids within their evolutionary environment\. Additionally, the MSA Transformer can predict inter\-residue contacts, which are crucial for understanding protein tertiary structure\. These predictions are derived from the attention weights learned during the axial self\-attention process, indicating residues that are likely to be spatially close\.

 To manage the computational demands of large MSAs, the [msa\_transformer\.py L21](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/msa_transformer.py#L21) class \(in [`esm/model/msa_transformer.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/msa_transformer.py)\) incorporates mechanisms like [msa\_transformer\.py L229](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/msa_transformer.py#L229) to dynamically adjust how attention computations are batched during inference\. This allows for processing larger inputs by breaking down attention calculations into smaller, more manageable chunks, thus optimizing memory usage\. The model also includes an [esm1\.py L24](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/model/esm1.py#L24) method, streamlining the configuration of its hyperparameters and promoting flexibility for various applications\.### Data Handling and Pre\-trained Model Loading

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The repository provides utilities for managing protein sequence data and loading pre\-trained models\. The core components for data handling are defined in [`esm/data.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py)\. The [data\.py L91](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L91) class handles the tokenization of protein sequences, defining the vocabulary of amino acids and special tokens, and mapping them to integer IDs\. This class is also responsible for configuring itself based on specific ESM model architectures, ensuring compatibility between tokenization and the model\.

 For loading sequence data, [data\.py L19](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L19) reads protein sequences from FASTA files\. It optimizes batching by grouping sequences of similar lengths to minimize padding, which is beneficial for GPU efficiency during model inference\. After sequences are loaded and tokenized, they are prepared for model input by either [data\.py L253](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L253) or [data\.py L300](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L300)\. The [data\.py L253](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L253) transforms a batch of raw sequence strings into padded [modules\.py L198](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/modules.py#L198)s of token IDs, incorporating special tokens like beginning\-of\-sequence \([data\.py L118](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L118)\) and end\-of\-sequence \([data\.py L120](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L120)\) as needed\. The [data\.py L300](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/data.py#L300) extends this functionality to handle Multiple Sequence Alignments \(MSAs\), ensuring that all sequences within an MSA are aligned and then processed into a 3D tensor suitable for models like the MSA Transformer\.

 Pre\-trained model loading is managed by [`esm/pretrained.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py)\. This module offers a unified interface for loading various pre\-trained ESM models \(e\.g\., ESM\-1b, ESM\-2, MSA Transformer, ESM\-IF1, ESMFold\) and their corresponding alphabets\. It can load models from either local paths or remote hubs, abstracting the details of model storage and versioning\. The module handles specific requirements for different model architectures, including state dictionary key mapping for compatibility between versions and optional loading of regression weights used for tasks like contact prediction\. Convenience functions are provided for directly loading specific model versions, streamlining the process of integrating pre\-trained models into applications\.### Advanced Inference Techniques

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

For large protein language models such as ESM\-2, efficient memory management and optimized inference are crucial, especially when dealing with long protein sequences or limited computational resources\. The repository employs several advanced techniques to address these challenges, primarily by leveraging [README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L334)'s [fold\.py L39](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py#L39) \([README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L334)\) with CPU offloading and granular control over batching and computation\.

 One of the key strategies for handling very large models, like [pretrained\.py L390](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L390), is the use of [README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L334) with CPU offloading\. This technique allows model parameters and optimizer states to reside in CPU memory and only be transferred to the GPU as needed during computation\. This significantly reduces the GPU memory footprint, enabling inference with models that would otherwise exceed GPU capacity\. The script [`examples/esm2_infer_fairscale_fsdp_cpu_offloading.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/esm2_infer_fairscale_fsdp_cpu_offloading.py) demonstrates this by initializing a distributed environment, loading the pre\-trained ESM\-2 model, and wrapping its layers using [README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L334) with [esm2\_infer\_fairscale\_fsdp\_cpu\_offloading\.py L25](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/esm2_infer_fairscale_fsdp_cpu_offloading.py#L25)\.

 To further optimize performance and memory, especially during representation extraction and structure prediction with ESMFold, two key parameters are utilized: [README\.md?plain=1 L241](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L241) and [README\.md?plain=1 L242](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L242)\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L241](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L241) argument, as seen in the [`scripts/fold.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py) script, limits the total number of tokens \(amino acids\) processed within a single batch\. This prevents out\-of\-memory errors by ensuring that batch sizes are dynamically adjusted based on sequence lengths\. Sequences are often sorted by length prior to batching to create more uniformly sized batches, which can improve throughput by reducing the need for excessive padding\.

 The [README\.md?plain=1 L242](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L242) parameter, also configurable in [`scripts/fold.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py), is used to optimize the memory footprint of axial attention mechanisms within the model\. Axial attention, which typically has a quadratic memory complexity with respect to sequence length \(O\(L^2\)\), can be made more memory\-efficient by processing sequences in chunks, thereby reducing its memory complexity to linear \(O\(L\)\)\. This allows for processing much longer sequences on available hardware\. The [fold\.py L66](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py#L66) function in [`scripts/fold.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py) is responsible for generating batches that adhere to the specified [README\.md?plain=1 L241](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L241) limit\. The overall workflow for structure prediction, including these optimizations, is orchestrated by the [fold\.py L125](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py#L125) function in [`scripts/fold.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py)\.## Protein 3D Structure Prediction

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The repository provides tools and models for predicting the three\-dimensional \(3D\) structures of proteins from their amino acid sequences, with a primary focus on the ESMFold model\. ESMFold integrates protein language models with sophisticated folding mechanisms to achieve accurate structure predictions\.

 The core of this functionality is the [esmfold\.py L50](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py#L50) model, defined in [`esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py)\. This model processes input amino acid sequences, first by generating rich sequence embeddings using an ESM language model\. These embeddings capture evolutionary and contextual information from the protein sequence\. The model then passes these representations to a [trunk\.py L110](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py#L110) module, which iteratively refines the sequence and pairwise residue representations\. This iterative refinement process, including a recycling mechanism, progressively builds a more accurate understanding of the protein's conformational space\.

 The [trunk\.py L110](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py#L110), implemented in [`esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py), is responsible for this iterative refinement\. It employs [tri\_self\_attn\_block\.py L25](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/tri_self_attn_block.py#L25)s \([`esm/esmfold/v1/tri_self_attn_block.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/tri_self_attn_block.py)\) to update both sequence\-level and residue\-pair\-level information\. These blocks are central to modeling the complex interactions within a protein\. Finally, the refined representations are fed into a Structure Module \(from OpenFold\) to predict the atomic coordinates, yielding the complete 3D protein structure\.

 Beyond structure prediction, ESMFold also estimates several quality metrics, including pLDDT \(Predicted Local Distance Difference Test\) scores, which indicate the model's confidence in local regions of the predicted structure, and pTM \(Predicted TM\-score\), which assesses the overall accuracy of the predicted global fold\. These metrics are crucial for evaluating the reliability of the predicted structures\.

 To facilitate practical application, the repository includes utilities for preparing input protein sequences and processing the model's output\. Functions in [`esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py) handle the encoding of amino acid strings into numerical tensors, including support for multi\-chain proteins\. After prediction, these utilities also convert the model's output into standard PDB \(Protein Data Bank\) format, enabling visualization and further analysis of the predicted structures\.

 The repository also offers access to various pre\-trained ESMFold models, as detailed in [`esm/esmfold/v1/pretrained.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/pretrained.py)\. These include different versions of the full ESMFold model and specialized "structure module only" baselines, which are valuable for research and development, allowing users to leverage models trained on extensive protein data for immediate application\.### ESMFold Architecture and Prediction Mechanism

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ESMFold model predicts protein 3D structures and associated quality metrics from amino acid sequences\. It integrates an ESM language model for sequence embeddings with a dedicated folding mechanism\. The overall architecture is defined in the [esmfold\.py L50](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py#L50) class in [`esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py), which orchestrates the prediction process\.

 The process begins by computing language model representations from input amino acid sequences using pre\-trained ESM models \(e\.g\., [esmfold\.py L36](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py#L36), [esmfold\.py L44](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py#L44)\)\. These representations, which capture sequence context, are then processed and fed into the [trunk\.py L110](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py#L110)\. The [trunk\.py L110](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py#L110), implemented in [`esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py), iteratively refines the sequence and pairwise representations of the protein state\. This iterative refinement includes a recycling mechanism where the outputs from one pass are fed back as inputs to subsequent passes, allowing the model to progressively refine its understanding of the protein's conformation\.

 Within each iteration of the [trunk\.py L110](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py#L110), [tri\_self\_attn\_block\.py L25](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/tri_self_attn_block.py#L25)s \(from [`esm/esmfold/v1/tri_self_attn_block.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/tri_self_attn_block.py)\) update both sequence and pairwise representations\. These blocks employ self\-attention and triangular attention mechanisms to capture intricate relationships between residues\. The refined representations are then passed to a [trunk\.py L11](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py#L11), which translates them into 3D atomic coordinates\.

 After the [trunk\.py L110](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py#L110) and [trunk\.py L11](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/trunk.py#L11) generate the initial structural predictions, various heads compute additional structural and quality metrics\. These include [esmfold\.py L234](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py#L234) for residue\-residue distances, [esmfold\.py L236](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py#L236) for sequence recovery, [esmfold\.py L99](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py#L99) for predicting pLDDT scores \(a measure of local structural accuracy\), and [esmfold\.py L96](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/esmfold.py#L96) for predicting pTM scores \(a measure of global structural accuracy, particularly for protein complexes\)\. The [categorical\_mixture\.py L8](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/categorical_mixture.py#L8) class in [`esm/esmfold/v1/categorical_mixture.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/categorical_mixture.py) is used to model categorical distributions for metrics like pLDDT\. The final predicted structures can be converted into PDB format using utilities in [`esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py) for visualization and further analysis\. For details on loading different model versions, see [Loading Pre\-trained ESMFold Models](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#protein-3d-structure-prediction-loading-pre-trained-esmfold-models)\.### Data Preparation and Output Processing for ESMFold

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Preparing amino acid sequences for ESMFold inference involves converting them into numerical representations and organizing them into batches, while processing the model's output typically involves converting predicted structures into the PDB format\. The [misc\.py L18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py#L18) function within [`esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py) handles the conversion of a single amino acid sequence string into numerical tensors, which includes mapping amino acids to integer types, generating residue indices, and creating masks for chain linkers\. For multi\-chain sequences, it can optionally insert chain linkers and assign chain indices\. The [misc\.py L61](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py#L61) function then processes a list of such sequences, collating their encoded representations into batched tensors\. This batching is managed by [misc\.py L119](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py#L119), which pads tensors of varying lengths to create a single stacked tensor suitable for model input\. After inference, the [misc\.py L93](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py#L93) function in [`esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/misc.py) is used to convert the model's output, such as predicted atom coordinates and residue types, into a list of PDB\-formatted strings for visualization and further analysis\. This utility leverages protein data handling conventions to ensure consistent representation\.### Loading Pre\-trained ESMFold Models

```
# Load a full ESMFold model
model_v1 = esmfold_v1()
# Model configuration and state are loaded internally.
# The model is ready for inference.

# Load a "structure module only" baseline model
model_structure_only = esmfold_structure_module_only_8M()
# This model uses the 8M parameter ESM-2 and 0 folding blocks.
# It's useful for analyzing the language model's capabilities in isolation.

# You can inspect the model's architecture or move it to a device
# print(model_v1)
# model_v1.to("cuda")
```

The process of loading pre\-trained ESMFold models is managed through dedicated functions within [`esm/esmfold/v1/pretrained.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/pretrained.py)\. This module provides utilities for accessing various versions of the ESMFold model, enabling users to either load models from local storage or download them from a remote URL\.

 At its core, the loading mechanism, handled by the internal [pretrained\.py L13](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/esmfold/v1/pretrained.py#L13) function, retrieves model configurations and pre\-trained weights\. This function is responsible for ensuring compatibility between the loaded weights and the model architecture, preventing issues that could arise from mismatched versions\.

 Specific functions like [pretrained\.py L400](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L400) and [README\.md?plain=1 L104](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L104) facilitate the loading of full ESMFold models, such as the one described in the original ESMFold publication\. Additionally, the module offers a range of "structure module only" baseline models \(e\.g\., [pretrained\.py L422](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L422), [pretrained\.py L542](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L542)\)\. These baseline models are designed for researchers interested in dissecting the contributions of different components or scaling parameters within the ESMFold architecture, often used for ablation studies where the language model's impact is varied by parameter count and training updates\.## Inverse Folding for Protein Design

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The repository includes tools and models for inverse folding, specifically the ESM\-IF1 model, which predicts protein sequences given a known 3D protein structure\. This process is fundamental for generative protein design, allowing researchers to explore novel sequences that can adopt a desired fold, and for scoring existing or designed sequences based on their likelihood of folding into a target structure\.

 The ESM\-IF1 model's core mechanism integrates Geometric Vector Perceptrons \(GVPs\) with a Transformer architecture\. GVPs are essential for processing the 3D structural information of proteins while maintaining rotational invariance, meaning the model's predictions are independent of the protein's global orientation in space\. These GVP\-encoded structural features are then fed into a Transformer decoder, which autoregressively predicts the amino acid sequence\. This design allows the model to effectively leverage both the geometric properties of the protein backbone and the contextual dependencies of amino acid sequences\. Further details on the model's internal architecture can be found in [ESM\-IF1 Model Architecture: GVP and Transformer Integration](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#inverse-folding-for-protein-design-esm-if1-model-architecture-gvp-and-transformer-integration)\.

 Practically, ESM\-IF1 facilitates two main applications: sequence sampling and scoring\. Sequence sampling involves generating novel protein sequences that are predicted to fold into a given 3D backbone\. This process is controlled by a temperature parameter, allowing adjustments to the diversity of the generated sequences\. Conversely, sequence scoring evaluates the log\-likelihood of a specific amino acid sequence for a given protein structure, providing a measure of how well that sequence "fits" the structure\. This is useful for validating designed sequences or evaluating natural variants\. Both applications support handling multi\-chain protein complexes, enabling design and analysis in the context of protein\-protein interactions\. For practical guidance on these applications, refer to [Practical Applications: Sequence Sampling and Scoring](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#inverse-folding-for-protein-design-practical-applications-sequence-sampling-and-scoring)\.### ESM\-IF1 Model Architecture: GVP and Transformer Integration

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ESM\-IF1 model is designed for inverse protein folding, predicting protein sequences given a 3D protein structure\. Its architecture integrates Geometric Vector Perceptrons \(GVPs\) with a Transformer for autoregressive sequence prediction\.

 The central component of the ESM\-IF1 architecture is the [gvp\_transformer\.py L24](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer.py#L24) in [`esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer.py)\. This model orchestrates the flow from structural input to sequence output\. It comprises an encoder, which processes the 3D structural information, and a decoder, which generates the amino acid sequence\.

 The structural input, consisting of protein coordinates, is first processed by the [gvp\_transformer\_encoder\.py L23](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer_encoder.py#L23) in [`esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer_encoder.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer_encoder.py)\. This encoder is crucial for converting geometric data into a suitable representation\. It employs [gvp\_encoder\.py L18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_encoder.py#L18) modules from [`esm/inverse_folding/gvp_encoder.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_encoder.py), which utilize Geometric Vector Perceptrons \(GVPs\) to handle 3D coordinate information\. GVPs are designed to preserve Euclidean invariances, making them effective for processing geometric data like protein structures\. This ensures that the model's output is independent of the global orientation of the input protein\. The [gvp\_transformer\_encoder\.py L23](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_transformer_encoder.py#L23) also incorporates dihedral angles and positional embeddings, combining these diverse features into a unified structural representation\. This initial embedding phase leverages components defined in [`esm/inverse_folding/features.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/features.py) for extracting node and edge features from 3D coordinates\.

 Once the structural features are encoded by the GVP\-enhanced encoder, these representations are passed to a [transformer\_decoder\.py L24](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/transformer_decoder.py#L24) in [`esm/inverse_folding/transformer_decoder.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/transformer_decoder.py)\. The decoder is a multi\-layer Transformer block responsible for autoregressively generating the protein sequence\. It takes the encoded structural context and predicts amino acids one by one, building the protein sequence\. This process is governed by standard Transformer decoder mechanisms, including self\-attention and encoder\-decoder attention\. The individual layers of both the encoder and decoder are implemented in [`esm/inverse_folding/transformer_layer.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/transformer_layer.py), which define the self\-attention and feed\-forward network components that form the backbone of the Transformer architecture\.

 The modules in [`esm/inverse_folding/gvp_modules.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_modules.py) provide the fundamental GVP layers and graph convolutional mechanisms, allowing the model to aggregate information from neighboring nodes in the protein's graph representation while preserving geometric properties\. Utility functions for handling graph data, such as [gvp\_utils\.py L9](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_utils.py#L9) and [gvp\_utils\.py L50](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_utils.py#L50) in [`esm/inverse_folding/gvp_utils.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/gvp_utils.py), facilitate efficient processing of graph\-structured data by the GVP components\.

 For practical applications, the model can sample new sequences or score existing ones\. See [Practical Applications: Sequence Sampling and Scoring](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#inverse-folding-for-protein-design-practical-applications-sequence-sampling-and-scoring) for more details\. The [util\.py L220](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/util.py#L220) in [`esm/inverse_folding/util.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/util.py) plays a role in preparing the input coordinates and sequences for batch processing, handling varying lengths and padding\. For complex structures with multiple chains, utilities in [`esm/inverse_folding/multichain_util.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/multichain_util.py) manage the extraction and concatenation of coordinates, allowing the model to operate on multi\-chain protein complexes\.### Practical Applications: Sequence Sampling and Scoring

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The ESM\-IF1 model provides capabilities for both generating novel protein sequences from a given 3D protein structure and evaluating the fitness of existing or designed sequences against a structure\. These functionalities are primarily exposed through command\-line scripts designed for practical protein design applications\.

 For **sampling protein sequences**, the script [`examples/inverse_folding/sample_sequences.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/inverse_folding/sample_sequences.py) allows users to generate new amino acid sequences that are predicted to fold into a specified protein backbone\. This is achieved by loading a pre\-trained ESM\-IF1 model and then performing multinomial sampling of amino acids at each position, conditioned on the provided structural coordinates\. The diversity of the sampled sequences can be controlled using a [optimize\.py L20](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/optimize.py#L20) parameter\. The tool supports conditioning on either a single protein chain or an entire multi\-chain protein complex\. When conditioning on a multi\-chain complex, the model takes into account the interactions and spatial relationships between all chains in the structure\. Sampled sequences are output in FASTA format, facilitating their use in further bioinformatics analyses\.

 For **scoring protein sequences**, the script [`examples/inverse_folding/score_log_likelihoods.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/inverse_folding/score_log_likelihoods.py) evaluates how well a given protein sequence aligns with a specific 3D structure by computing its conditional log\-likelihood\. This can be used to assess the "fitness" of a native sequence or to score designed variants against a target structure\. The script loads the ESM\-IF1 model and calculates log\-likelihoods for both the native sequence of a structure and a set of user\-provided variant sequences\. Like sequence sampling, scoring can be performed for single\-chain structures or in the context of multi\-chain complexes, where the model considers the entire complex backbone\. The results, including log\-likelihood scores and perplexity, are typically output in a CSV format\.

 Both sampling and scoring functionalities rely on utility functions in [`esm/inverse_folding/util.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/util.py) and [`esm/inverse_folding/multichain_util.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/inverse_folding/multichain_util.py) for tasks such as loading protein structures \(PDB or CIF files\), extracting N, CA, C atom coordinates, and preparing data for model input\. The ability to handle multi\-chain complexes is particularly important for designing or evaluating sequences within the context of protein\-protein interactions or larger biological assemblies\.## Example Applications and Tutorials

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This section provides practical scripts and examples demonstrating various applications of protein language models\. These examples cover diverse use cases, including large model inference, generative protein design with integrated structural and sequence considerations, and zero\-shot variant prediction, offering guidance for researchers to apply these models effectively\.

 For large model inference, the [`examples/esm2_infer_fairscale_fsdp_cpu_offloading.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/esm2_infer_fairscale_fsdp_cpu_offloading.py) script illustrates how to run inference with substantial ESM\-2 models, such as [pretrained\.py L390](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/esm/pretrained.py#L390)\. This script is particularly useful for managing memory constraints, as it employs [README\.md?plain=1 L334](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L334)'s [fold\.py L39](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/scripts/fold.py#L39) \(FSDP\) with CPU offloading\. This technique allows model parameters to reside primarily in CPU memory and be moved to the GPU only when necessary, enabling the use of models that would otherwise exceed GPU capacity\. The process involves initializing a distributed environment, loading the pre\-trained model, and wrapping its layers with FSDP for efficient memory management during inference to generate representations and contact predictions\.

 For generative protein design, two frameworks are highlighted\. The first is [README\.md?plain=1 L5](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L5), located in the [`examples/lm-design`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design) directory\. This framework supports both fixed backbone design, where a sequence is optimized for an existing protein structure, and free generation, where sequences are generated de novo\. The core of [README\.md?plain=1 L5](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L5) is the [lm\_design\.py L54](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/lm_design.py#L54) class in [`examples/lm-design/lm_design.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/lm_design.py), which integrates language model embeddings with structural prediction\. It optimizes sequences using a composite loss function that can include sequence likelihood, structural contacts, and n\-gram distributions\. The framework uses Hydra for flexible configuration, enabling researchers to define custom optimization schedules and balance different loss components\. Details on its architecture and mechanisms can be found in [Generative Protein Design with Language Models \(LM\-Design\)](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#example-applications-and-tutorials-generative-protein-design-with-language-models-lm-design)\. The second framework is a Protein Programming Language, located in [`examples/protein-programming-language`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language)\. This domain\-specific language facilitates generative protein design by allowing users to define energy terms, specify folding simulations \(e\.g\., using [folding\_callbacks\.py L43](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/folding_callbacks.py#L43) from [`examples/protein-programming-language/language/folding_callbacks.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/folding_callbacks.py)\), and apply optimization algorithms like simulated annealing via [optimize\.py L93](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/optimize.py#L93) in [`examples/protein-programming-language/language/optimize.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/optimize.py)\. The fundamental building block is the [program\.py L18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/program.py#L18) class from [`examples/protein-programming-language/language/program.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/program.py), which supports hierarchical program definitions and sequence manipulation using [sequence\.py L64](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/sequence.py#L64) from [`examples/protein-programming-language/language/sequence.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/sequence.py)\. This language is designed to enable the creation of diverse design programs, from fixed\-backbone sequence optimization to free hallucination and scaffolding around functional sites\. Further details are provided in [Protein Programming Language for De Novo Design](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#example-applications-and-tutorials-protein-programming-language-for-de-novo-design)\.

 Zero\-shot variant prediction is addressed by the scripts in [`examples/variant-prediction`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/variant-prediction)\. The [README\.md?plain=1 L10](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/variant-prediction/README.md?plain=1#L10) script in this directory utilizes models like ESM\-1v and MSA Transformer to predict the functional effects of mutations from deep mutational scanning data\. It supports various scoring strategies, such as [README\.md?plain=1 L17](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/variant-prediction/README.md?plain=1#L17) and [README\.md?plain=1 L29](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/variant-prediction/README.md?plain=1#L29), depending on the model used\. For MSA\-based models, it can process multiple sequence alignments, allowing researchers to evaluate how mutations might impact protein function without requiring experimental data for each variant\. The [`examples/variant-prediction/README.md`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/variant-prediction/README.md) file in this directory also points to pre\-computed performance data from a research paper, allowing for validation and comparison of predictions\.### Generative Protein Design with Language Models \(LM\-Design\)

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The [README\.md?plain=1 L5](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L5) framework, located in [`examples/lm-design`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design), provides tools for designing protein sequences using language models\. It supports two main design approaches: fixed backbone design, where a sequence is optimized for a given protein structure, and free generation, which creates both the structure and sequence simultaneously\. The framework integrates structural and sequence\-based loss functions and uses configurable optimization schedules to guide the design process\.

 At the core of this framework is the [lm\_design\.py L54](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/lm_design.py#L54) class, defined in [`examples/lm-design/lm_design.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/lm_design.py)\. This class manages model initialization, calculates various loss components, and executes design tasks\. It leverages a language model to evaluate the likelihood of sequences and a structural model to predict 3D features, such as inter\-residue distances and angles\. The [lm\_design\.py L54](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/lm_design.py#L54) computes a combined loss function that can include a sequence loss \(assessing the negative log\-likelihood of the designed sequence under the language model\), a structure loss \(evaluating how well the predicted structure aligns with a target or desired properties\), and an n\-gram loss \(penalizing unusual amino acid n\-gram distributions\)\. These loss components are weighted and combined to optimize the design\.

 Design tasks, such as fixed backbone design, implemented through [fixedbb\.py L18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/utils/fixedbb.py#L18) in [`examples/lm-design/utils/fixedbb.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/utils/fixedbb.py), and free generation, orchestrated by [free\_generation\.py L22](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/utils/free_generation.py#L22) in [`examples/lm-design/utils/free_generation.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/lm-design/utils/free_generation.py), involve iterative refinement\. For example, fixed backbone design uses a Metropolis\-Hastings sampling method to propose amino acid mutations and accepts or rejects them based on the combined loss function\. The free generation process iteratively resamples target structures using the structural model and then designs sequences to fit these new structures, enabling the de novo creation of both sequence and corresponding structure\.

 Configuration for the [README\.md?plain=1 L5](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/README.md?plain=1#L5) framework is managed using Hydra, allowing for flexible and reproducible experimentation through external YAML files\. This enables users to easily adjust design parameters, model weights, and task types without modifying the core code\. The framework also includes utilities for managing random number generation states, which ensures reproducible sampling, and for processing protein data from PDB files, which is essential for defining target structures or evaluating generated designs\. For more information on how structural models are loaded and used within this framework, refer to [Protein 3D Structure Prediction](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#protein-3d-structure-prediction)\.### Protein Programming Language for De Novo Design

![Diagram](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

This domain\-specific language provides a framework for generative protein design, enabling the exploration of novel protein sequences and structures through an evolutionary search process\. It integrates components for defining design objectives, simulating protein folding, and optimizing designs\.

 At its core, the language is built around the [program\.py L18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/program.py#L18) class, which serves as a fundamental building block for representing protein design tasks\. A [program\.py L18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/program.py#L18) can define either a specific [sequence\.py L64](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/sequence.py#L64) that produces a protein sequence or can act as a parent node containing other [program\.py L18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/program.py#L18) instances, allowing for the hierarchical definition of protein complexes or domains\. This modularity supports both simple and complex protein constructs\.

 Protein designs are evaluated using [energy\.py L16](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/energy.py#L16) objects\. These objects calculate a score based on various structural and quality metrics from a [folding\_callbacks\.py L22](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/folding_callbacks.py#L22)\. Examples include [energy\.py L25](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/energy.py#L25) for overall structural accuracy, [energy\.py L34](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/energy.py#L34) for local structure confidence, [energy\.py L43](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/energy.py#L43) for enforcing symmetry in protein assemblies, and [energy\.py L102](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/energy.py#L102) for promoting solubility\. These terms can be weighted to prioritize specific design goals\.

 The [sequence\.py L64](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/sequence.py#L64) interface handles protein sequence generation and manipulation\. Implementations like [sequence\.py L81](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/sequence.py#L81) allow for fixed, unchangeable regions \(e\.g\., a functional binding site\), while [sequence\.py L96](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/sequence.py#L96) and [sequence\.py L146](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/sequence.py#L146) enable the design of regions with constant or variable lengths, respectively, accommodating mutations, insertions, and deletions during the design process\.

 Protein folding simulations are facilitated by the [folding\_callbacks\.py L28](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/folding_callbacks.py#L28) interface, with [folding\_callbacks\.py L43](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/folding_callbacks.py#L43) providing a concrete implementation using the ESMFold v1\.0 model\. This component takes a protein sequence and predicts its 3D structure, along with quality metrics such as predicted TM\-score \(pTM\) and predicted local distance difference test \(pLDDT\)\. These metrics are encapsulated in a [folding\_callbacks\.py L22](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/folding_callbacks.py#L22) object and are used by [energy\.py L16](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/energy.py#L16) objects for evaluation\.

 The optimization process leverages a [optimize\.py L93](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/optimize.py#L93) algorithm, which employs Metropolis\-Hastings steps to explore the vast space of possible protein designs\. This algorithm iteratively mutates [program\.py L18](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/program.py#L18) instances, evaluates the energy of the resulting protein structures using the defined [energy\.py L16](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/language/energy.py#L16) objects, and probabilistically accepts or rejects changes to converge towards optimal designs\. This approach allows for the discovery of novel sequences that meet desired structural and functional criteria\.

 A variety of example design programs demonstrate the language's capabilities\. These include programs for fixed backbone design \(e\.g\., [`examples/protein-programming-language/programs/fixed_backbone.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/programs/fixed_backbone.py)\), free hallucination of novel proteins \(e\.g\., [`examples/protein-programming-language/programs/free_hallucination.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/programs/free_hallucination.py)\), scaffolding functional sites \(e\.g\., [`examples/protein-programming-language/programs/functional_site_scaffolding.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/programs/functional_site_scaffolding.py)\), and designing symmetric assemblies such as monomers, multimers, and proteins with multiple binding sites \(e\.g\., [`examples/protein-programming-language/programs/symmetric_monomer.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/programs/symmetric_monomer.py), [`examples/protein-programming-language/programs/symmetric_two_level_multimer.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/programs/symmetric_two_level_multimer.py), [`examples/protein-programming-language/programs/symmetric_binding.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/programs/symmetric_binding.py)\)\. Additionally, designs for controlling secondary structure elements are provided \(e\.g\., [`examples/protein-programming-language/programs/secondary_structure.py`](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm/blob/2b369911bb5b4b0dda914521b9475cad1656b2ac/examples/protein-programming-language/programs/secondary_structure.py)\)\. More information on applications can be found in [Example Applications and Tutorials](https://codewiki.google/github.com/facebookresearch/esm#example-applications-and-tutorials)\.## ESM Metagenomic Atlas
